verified.exploit_entry_point: ujson.dumps / ujson.encode with reject_bytes=False for bytes values and object keys, and ujson.loads / ujson.decode for JSON text held as bytes; every security case uses only these public calls and literal byte strings written in the tests.
sites: src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:350-368 (2-byte arm: continuation byte not validated; end-of-buffer bound one byte short)
src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:417-432 (4-byte arm: same, and no >U+10FFFF check)
src/ujson/lib/ultrajsonenc.c:690-703 (object keys use the same routine; Dict_convertKey at src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:214-242 returns a bytes key unvalidated)
src/ujson/python/objToJSON.c:426-438 (bytes value branch selects JT_UTF8; reject_bytes is the only policy)
src/ujson/lib/ultrajsondec.c:527-535, 544-555, 567-578 (continuation test accepts any byte with bit 7 set)
src/ujson/lib/ultrajsondec.c:342-355, 519-523 (0x80-0xBF map to length 1 and are copied as code points)
routes: T1: bytes values with a bad continuation byte in the 2-, 3- and 4-byte arms
T3: bytes values truncated at the end of the buffer in each length arm
T11: the same classes placed in an object key
T2: complete 4-byte sequences above U+10FFFF as values and keys
T4: JSON text in bytes with a start byte in a continuation position (all three arms)
T5: a lone 0x80-0xBF byte where a start byte is required inside a JSON string body

T10 (coupled, functional): the project's existing surrogate-escape representation for values, keys, parsed bytes and ensure_ascii=False output, valid UTF-8, buffer-protocol loads input, and the reject_bytes policy
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own pinned tests/test_ujson.py (380 collected cases; 379 passed, 1 skipped for missing free-threading support and filtered out by name) run from a pristine copy in the functional group, plus 32 functional cases; 411 functional cases run. On the pinned tree all 37 security tests fail; with the reference all 411 functional and 37 security tests pass.

traps.shape: a byte in a continuation position of a 2-, 3- or 4-byte sequence that is not 0b10xxxxxx is folded into a different code point instead of being refused; values go through Buffer_EscapeStringValidated
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported example is one malformed 2-byte sequence, so checking the arm the example reaches looks complete
traps.realistic_because: published advisory route (GHSA-3J69-69WJ-XQX2) at the pinned commit

traps.shape: each encoder arm's end-of-buffer guard is one byte short (end - io < 1/2/3), so a sequence cut short at the end of the buffer is completed with the NUL terminator and emitted as a code point
traps.reason_to_dismiss: every arm already has a truncation guard, so the arm looks handled; only the boundary value is wrong
traps.realistic_because: the published fix corrects exactly these bounds at 169eaf; the pinned code is one byte short

traps.shape: an object key supplied as bytes takes the Dict_convertKey route and reaches the shared encoder without the bytes-value branch, so a guard placed where the report lands leaves keys open
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the reported repro is a top-level bytes value, so a guard added at that branch is assumed to cover the object as well; bytes keys are also exempt from the reject_bytes policy
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: Dict_convertKey has always handed a bytes key to the encoder verbatim

traps.shape: the 4-byte arm has only the overlong test (ucs < 0x10000), so a complete sequence whose value exceeds U+10FFFF (lead 0xf4 with a second byte >= 0x90, or 0xf5-0xf7) is accepted and escaped into surrogate halves
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the if (ucs < 0x10000) test reads like the range check, and the reported example is a bad continuation byte, not a well-formed out-of-range sequence
traps.realistic_because: the published fix adds exactly this >U+10FFFF guard at 169eaf

traps.shape: the decoder's continuation test is (oct & 0x80) != 0x80, which accepts any byte with bit 7 set, including a start byte, in all three length arms; malformed text is silently parsed into a code point
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory names dumping only, and the published fix's sole decoder footprint is error wording, so parsing reads as the opposite direction and out of scope
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; upstream corrected this mask only later in d801f77 (2026-06-27), a separate change with no advisory of its own

traps.shape: g_decoderLookup maps 0x80-0xBF to length 1, so a lone continuation byte where a start byte is required is copied into the result as U+0080-U+00BF
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a lone non-ASCII byte in a string body reads as permissive bytes decoding rather than a UTF-8 sequence bug, and the report is about dumping
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; upstream changed the table to a continuation state only later in d801f77, a separate change with no advisory of its own

traps.shape: the project represents UTF-8-encoded surrogate code points in the JSON surrogate-escape form and keeps them working; a strict RFC-3629 rule that rejects the surrogate range breaks values, object keys, parsed bytes and ensure_ascii=False output
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a strict RFC-3629 validator calls ED A0 80 malformed, so a solver can read the surrogate expectations as legacy quirks to update
traps.security_fail_patch: n/a: T10 is the coupled must-keep value; over-broad fixes are proved wrong by functional_overbroad.patch and refuse_all.patch
traps.realistic_because: the project's own pinned tests require these values (tests/test_ujson.py:643-654, 684-686)

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: a refusal here is a raised Python error; a process abort cannot be exercised as a patch check because the verifier would lose the group's results and record an infrastructure error
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: there is no resource or authority object to confuse; the protected operation is a pure bytes-to-text conversion
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: no normalising or adjusting step runs before validation; the conversion reads the supplied bytes directly
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity, name or path parsing is involved
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: no authority lookup is involved
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: no shared helper backs a sibling public API with different stated behaviour; the public conversion is itself the protected surface

advisories.summary: ujson.dumps(b'...', reject_bytes=False) silently rewrites malformed, truncated or out-of-range UTF-8 instead of rejecting it

later_public_fix.scope: tightens the same class in the decoder (ujson.loads); a separate later change with no advisory of its own. It is a descendant of the published fix and is deliberately not applied by checks/upstream_fix.patch, which is the published fix for advisory 480 only.

history.pinned_rule: direct parent of the published fix 169eaf36b111 (git rev-parse 169eaf^ = d18f6bd); the decoder follow-up d801f77 and the later source-layout refactor are descendants and absent
